rubrics.justification: Generally consistent with a good-quality blastocyst, but it hedges against the reported 3AA and includes uncertain image-based claims such as intact/not significantly thinned zona and early-to-full blastocyst wording despite lab grade of expanded blastocyst.
Integrates age, ovarian reserve, BMI, semen, endometrium, endometriosis, and prior ectopic history well with embryo prognosis, though some links are somewhat generalized.

Overall logical and structured, but there are minor inconsistencies such as calling 11 mm endometrium favorable yet also suggesting it may indicate pathology, and implying concern from thickness alone.

Recommendations are largely evidence-based: SET for a young patient with a high-grade blastocyst, standard luteal support, cavity/tubal evaluation after ectopic, and no routine PGT-A at age 30. Minor overinterpretation of endometrial thickness prevents a top score.

Provides practical next steps for transfer and future planning, including SET, luteal support, cavity assessment, and hydrosalpinx evaluation, though some recommendations remain conditional rather than highly specific.
